description: Pins the person-derived account number: the leading 95 bits of the big-endian 16-byte person id, encoded five bits at a time most-significant-first through the Crockford alphabet, plus the frozen Damm-32 check character over the 19 indices. The alphabet, the check character, the display grouping and the account_number_hash rule are unchanged from account-number.md §2 to §6; only the bit source differs from a generated number. `input_person_id_hex` is the normative input, `input_phrase` is informational so a port can pin the phrase-to-id hop too.

cases.description: The phrase the person-keypair family already pins. The top 95 bits of its person id, five bits at a time most-significant-first, plus the Damm-32 check digit.
A different phrase, so the family cannot pass by ignoring its input.
All-zero person id: the canonical body is twenty `0` characters (the Damm-32 check over nineteen zero indices is zero).
Only bit 127 set. The leading five-bit group carries index 16 (`G`) and the rest are zero; a reader that took the LOW 95 bits would emit all zeros here instead.
Only bits 0..=32 set, all of them outside the window. Must produce the all-zero canonical body; a mask that kept the low 95 bits would not.
